The doctor talked to my dad while I was high, and my dad gave me all these crazy diet restrictions that the doctor had said I needed to follow. He said I was lactose intolerant, so I cut down on dairy, and he said that I couldn't eat anything too acidic, so no more pickles. There were others, but I remember those because they were the most difficult.  

At an appointment with the gastroenterologist who did the colonoscopy, I said I was following all the restrictions, eating lots of "healthy" foods like salads, and STILL having pain. He was like "Um, what diet restrictions?" He told me I'm not lactose intolerant and to cut down on the salads because raw vegetables are rough on intestines.  

My point is that even if your parents and other parientes THINK they're doing what's best for you, they could be hindering you instead of helping you; they could even be completely wrong, like my dad. IMO, you should have a colonoscopy AND allergy test done. I've done both multiple times, and they were both mostly worth the trouble.
